title: runtime/scheduler: two-queue dispatch (short-first) w/ fairness window + microbench
author: Marcus Reed
release_notes: Adds a feature-flagged two-queue scheduler dispatch mode (short-first) with a fairness window to reduce tail latency in mixed prompt workloads; includes microbench coverage.
description:
Context: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (ENG-4821 umbrella). This PR implements the core dispatch policy for a two-queue scheduler: requests are classified upstream (see PR #8427) as SHORT vs LONG and enqueued into separate ready queues. The dispatcher serves SHORT preferentially while enforcing a fairness window so LONG work continues to make progress under bursty interactive traffic.

Why: In mixed traffic (chatty short prompts + occasional long-context summarization), FIFO batching tends to let long-prefill jobs inflate the wait time for short requests and drive p95/p99 regressions. We want to prioritize latency-sensitive SHORT traffic without allowing LONG to starve (and without tanking throughput).

What this PR does:
- Adds TwoQueueDispatchPolicy behind the existing scheduler flag plumbing (PR #8421). Default remains unchanged (FIFO) unless flag is enabled.
- Implements short-first dispatch with a fairness window based on a configurable service budget: after serving up to `short_service_budget_tokens` worth of SHORT work (measured as estimated prefill+decode tokens scheduled), the scheduler must attempt a LONG dispatch if a LONG request is ready. This prevents pathological long starvation during sustained SHORT bursts.
- Uses conservative estimates for token cost: prompt_tokens + max_output_tokens (until we have observed service-time based costing; follow-up PRs add better costing + guardrails).
- Handles streaming vs non-streaming uniformly at dispatch time; the queue selection is based on class only (streaming affects batch formation downstream).
- Adds microbench tests + a lightweight simulation harness to validate: (1) SHORT priority reduces mean/p95 wait vs FIFO for mixed arrivals, (2) LONG sees bounded delay (no infinite starvation in sustained SHORT arrival patterns), (3) scheduler stability under bursty enqueue patterns.

Algorithm details (as implemented):
- Maintain `short_budget_remaining_tokens` initialized to `short_service_budget_tokens`.
- On each dispatch decision:
  - If SHORT queue non-empty and `short_budget_remaining_tokens > 0`, dispatch from SHORT; decrement budget by estimated tokens for the dispatched request/batch.
  - Else, if LONG queue non-empty, dispatch from LONG and reset budget to `short_service_budget_tokens`.
  - Else, if only SHORT exists, dispatch from SHORT (budget can go negative; it will force LONG as soon as one becomes available).
- If both queues are empty: no-op.

Notes / follow-ups:
- Starvation guardrails (explicit max wait bound metrics + periodic long-queue service under overload) are in #8439.
- Separate admission control thresholds per class are in #8462.
- Improved classifier costing using observed prefill time EWMA is in #8480.

Bench (local, A100-80G, llama-3.1-70b-ish internal profile, synthetic mix 80/20 short/long; N=5 runs; warm caches):
- SHORT p95 end-to-end latency: -14% to -21% vs FIFO (median -18%).
- SHORT p99: -10% to -16%.
- Throughput (tokens/s): -0.8% to -2.3% (median -1.5%).
- LONG p95: +2% to +6% depending on burstiness; still within current prototype targets; additional fairness tuning in follow-ups.

Rollout: feature-flagged only; default off. Intended for perf-canary A/B once the metrics PR (#8444) lands.

runtime/scheduler: add queue selection tests (determinism + fairness cases)
bench/micro: add mixed workload scheduler microbench scenarios
docs: inline comments + config examples for policy knobs
conversation:
Sofia Ivanova (review): Can you clarify the fairness guarantee? With the token budget approach, a burst of SHORT could still run indefinitely if LONG arrives right after we pick SHORT and then keep picking SHORT because budget stays >0. How do we ensure we eventually select LONG?

Marcus Reed (author): Yep. The budget monotonically decreases with each SHORT dispatch. Once it hits <=0, we will prefer LONG whenever LONG is present. If LONG arrives while budget is still positive, it may wait until the budget is consumed, but it cannot wait forever unless we stop decrementing budget (we always decrement by estimated tokens for dispatched SHORT). I added a unit test for: continuous SHORT arrivals + single LONG arrival => LONG dispatched once budget crosses <=0.

Lena Fischer (review): The decrement uses prompt_tokens + max_output_tokens. That seems pessimistic and might flip to LONG too often (hurting SHORT p95). Any plan to use observed prefill/decode service time instead?

Marcus Reed (author): Agree it’s pessimistic; chosen for safety while classifier costing is still conservative. Follow-up #8480 refines using observed prefill time EWMA and clamps. Also #8444 adds per-class wait/service metrics so we can tune `short_service_budget_tokens` empirically.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Microbench: can we add a case for burst oscillation (e.g., 200 SHORT at t=0, then 20 LONG at t=50ms)? I’ve seen schedulers thrash there.

Marcus Reed (author): Added `burst_oscillation_200s_20l` scenario and a regression assertion on SHORT p95 vs FIFO. Also added a trace log in the bench output for first 200 dispatches to make it debuggable.

Hiro Tanaka (review): Any risk this changes kernel selection or batch formation behavior enough to confound perf results? The dispatcher now alternates classes; are we accidentally forcing smaller prefills?

Marcus Reed (author): We’re not changing batch formation logic (still happens in batch_builder); this only influences which request enters the batch builder next. That said, alternating can reduce prefill batch size for LONG in some mixes; we’ll measure. I added a comment in the bench doc noting this as a confounder; the perf plan doc calls out watching GPU util and prefill batch sizes.

Sean Gallagher (review): From an ops/SRE perspective: I’m okay with default-off, but please ensure knobs have safe bounds. I don’t want someone setting budget to 1e12 and effectively starving long jobs.

Marcus Reed (author): Added config validation: budget must be in [1k, 5M] tokens; invalid values fall back to default (250k) and log a warning. Starvation alerting will land in #8444/#8439.

Outcome: Approved by Sofia/Lena/Omar; merged (squash) into main. Flag remains default-off; ready for metrics + guardrails follow-ups.
